    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
    | where Subject contains "従業員持株会"
        or Subject contains "人事異動"
        or Subject contains "給与改定"
        or Subject contains "給与調整"
        or Subject contains "税務コンプライアンス"
        or Subject contains "罰金通知"
        or Subject contains "持株会規約"
    | project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, AuthenticationDetails;
let UrlSide = SuspectMail
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailUrlInfo
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where UrlDomain has_any ("gofile.io","wetransfer.com","we.tl")
        | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain, UrlLocation
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | extend Vector = strcat("URL:", UrlDomain), Indicator = Url;

        | project NetworkMessageId, FileName, FileType, SHA256, FileSize

let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMin = 120;
let BombingThreshold = 5;
// MFA-friction failure codes per Entra docs
let MfaFailCodes = dynamic([500121, 50074, 50076, 50097, 50158]);
let Bombed = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where ErrorCode in (MfaFailCodes)
    | summarize FailCount = count(),
                FirstFail = min(Timestamp),
                LastFail  = max(Timestamp),
                SourceIPs = make_set(IPAddress, 25),
                SourceCountries = make_set(Country, 10)
                by AccountUpn, AccountObjectId
    | where FailCount >= BombingThreshold;
let MFAReg = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where ApplicationId == 11161  // Office 365 / Azure AD audit feed
    | where ActionType has_any ("User registered security info",
                                "Admin registered security info",
                                "User registered all required security info",
                                "User started security info registration",
                                "Update user")
    | extend TargetUpn = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ActivityObjects))[0].name)
    | where isnotempty(TargetUpn)
    | project RegTime = Timestamp, TargetUpn, ActionType, RegIP = IPAddress,
              ActorDisplayName = AccountDisplayName;
Bombed
| join kind=inner MFAReg on $left.AccountUpn == $right.TargetUpn
| where RegTime between (LastFail .. LastFail + WindowMin * 1m)
| project AccountUpn, FailCount, FirstFail, LastFail, RegTime,
          MinutesAfterBombing = datetime_diff('minute', RegTime, LastFail),
          ActionType, RegIP, SourceIPs, SourceCountries
| order by RegTime desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — kubernetes-el Compromised: How a Pwn Request Exploited a Popular Emacs Package
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("funny.sh", "memdump.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/secrets") or FileName in~ ("funny.sh", "memdump.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

3362.def:
// CVE-2026-25545 — Astro Node server egressing to external host fetching /404.html or /500.html
let astro_hosts = dynamic(["node.exe","node"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (astro_hosts)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","HttpConnectionInspected","ConnectionAttempt")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/404.html","/500.html") or RemotePort in (80, 443)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("astro","@astrojs/node","dist/server","server/entry.mjs")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
3362.sent:
// CVE-2026-25545 — Node.js (Astro SSR) egress fetch for /404.html or /500.html with UA 'node'
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent in~ ("node","node-fetch","undici")
   or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent startswith "node/"
   or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent startswith "undici/"
| where Url has_any ("/404.html","/500.html")
| where not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
   and not(DstIpAddr startswith "127.")
   and not(DstIpAddr startswith "169.254.")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7a8c1d9e-3b4f-4d6e-9a2c-5e8f1c2d4a6b
status: experimental
description: Detects the outbound HTTP fetch that the Astro SSR engine emits when its prerenderedErrorPageFetch() is hijacked by a spoofed Host header (CVE-2026-25545). The Node.js fetch() egresses with default User-Agent 'node' for /404.html or /500.html.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/astro-full-read-ssrf-via-host-header-injection
  - https://github.com/withastro/astro/security/advisories/GHSA-qq67-mvv5-fw3g
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-25545
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1133
  - cve.2026.25545
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'GET'
  selection_ua:
    c-useragent|startswith:
      - 'node'
      - 'undici'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|endswith:
      - '/404.html'
      - '/500.html'
  condition: selection_method and selection_ua and selection_uri

  - Internal monitoring scripts written in Node.js that probe error pages
  - Legitimate Node-based crawlers (rare; usually have a custom UA)

3363.sent:
// CVE-2026-25545 — Astro origin receiving requests with non-canonical Host header that yield 404/500
let _expected_hosts = dynamic(["www.example.com","example.com","astro.example.com"]); // tune per tenant
let AppService = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ScStatus in (404, 500)
    | extend HostOnly = tolower(tostring(split(CsHost, ":")[0]))
    | where isnotempty(HostOnly)
    | where HostOnly !in~ (_expected_hosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppServiceHTTPLogs", HostHeader=CsHost, ClientIP=CIp, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Status=ScStatus, UA=UserAgent, _ResourceId;
let Proxy = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("404","500") or toint(EventOutcome) in (404,500)
    | extend HostOnly = tolower(tostring(split(DestinationHostName, ":")[0]))
    | where isnotempty(HostOnly)
    | where HostOnly !in~ (_expected_hosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", HostHeader=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=toint(EventOutcome), UA=RequestClientApplication, _ResourceId;
union isfuzzy=true AppService, Proxy
| summarize Count=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), SampleUris=make_set(Uri, 10), SampleUAs=make_set(UA, 5), ClientIPs=make_set(ClientIP, 20) by HostHeader, Status, Source

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Securing the Agent Skill Ecosystem: How Snyk and Vercel Are Locking Down the New
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("skills.sh"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("skills.sh"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

3377.def:
// Qix npm phishing — sender domain npmjs.help (legitimate domain is npmjs.com)
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let PhishDomains = dynamic(["npmjs.help"]);
let MailHits =
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where SenderMailFromDomain in~ (PhishDomains)
       or SenderFromDomain in~ (PhishDomains)
       or SenderMailFromAddress endswith "@npmjs.help"
       or SenderFromAddress endswith "@npmjs.help"
    | project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              SenderMailFromAddress, SenderFromAddress, Subject,
              DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes, UrlCount;
let UrlHits =
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Url has "npmjs.help"
    | project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain;
MailHits
| join kind=leftouter UrlHits on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderMailFromAddress,
          SenderFromAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation,
          ThreatTypes, Url, NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc

3432.def:
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor stage-2 — UevAppMonitor.exe is a legitimate Windows binary that *only* ships in System32. Execution from anywhere else (especially Microsoft.NET\Framework) means a copy was staged by the dropper to side-load SharedReg.dll via AppDomainManager.
let UevExec =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "UevAppMonitor.exe"
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\")
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256;
let SharedRegLoad =
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "UevAppMonitor.exe"
    | where FileName =~ "SharedReg.dll"
    | where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
UevExec
| union SharedRegLoad
| order by Timestamp desc

3434.def:
// LongNosedGoblin NosyDoor dropper — writes a known set of artefacts into C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework so the relocated UevAppMonitor.exe loads SharedReg.dll via .config-driven AppDomainManager injection.
let NosyDoorFiles = dynamic([
    "SharedReg.dll",
    "log.cached",
    "netfxsbs9.hkf",            // typo of legitimate netfxsbs12.hkf
    "UevAppMonitor.exe.config",
    "UevAppMonitor.exe",         // staged copy from System32
    "error.txt"                  // dropped on stage-2 decryption errors
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ (@"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework", @"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64")
   or FolderPath endswith @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework"
   or FolderPath endswith @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64"
| where FileName in~ (NosyDoorFiles)
// Exclude legitimate .NET servicing — the genuine SharedReg DLL is named SharedReg12.dll, not SharedReg.dll
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "msiexec.exe", "setup.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\")
| summarize FileSet = make_set(FileName), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Writers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName)
  by DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(FileSet) >= 2     // at least two of the four sibling artefacts
| order by LastSeen desc

ImFileEvent

  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_verb:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' install '
      - ' add '
      - ' i '
  selection_pkg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'vointea'
      - 'voinzaril'
      - '-wekto'
      - '-riris'
      - '-z3n'
      - '-kyuki'
      - '-breki'
      - '-notthedevs'
      - 'ksni-technical-test'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_verb and selection_pkg
falsepositives:
  - Security researchers reproducing the incident in sandboxes
  - Threat-intel teams pulling sample packages for triage
level: medium
3478.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*install*" OR Processes.process="* add *" OR Processes.process="* i *") AND (Processes.process="*vointea*" OR Processes.process="*voinzaril*" OR Processes.process="*-wekto*" OR Processes.process="*-riris*" OR Processes.process="*-z3n*" OR Processes.process="*-kyuki*" OR Processes.process="*-breki*" OR Processes.process="*-notthedevs*" OR Processes.process="*ksni-technical-test*") by host Processes.user Processes.dest Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
3478.datadog: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\npx.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\npx.exe)) @CommandLine:(*install* OR *" add "* OR *" i "*) @CommandLine:(*vointea* OR *voinzaril* OR *-wekto* OR *-riris* OR *-z3n* OR *-kyuki* OR *-breki* OR *-notthedevs* OR *ksni-technical-test*)
3478.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/(npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i
| regex("(install|\\sadd\\s|\\si\\s)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| regex("(vointea|voinzaril|-(wekto|riris|z3n|kyuki|breki|notthedevs)|ksni-technical-test)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

3481.sigma:
title: WinRAR Drops File to User Startup Folder (CVE-2025-8088 Exploitation)
id: 7f1b6e3a-2c41-4e9b-a3b8-1f4d9c5e08a2
status: experimental
description: Detects WinRAR/UnRAR writing a file into the per-user Startup folder, the canonical persistence drop observed when CVE-2025-8088 (path traversal via Alternate Data Streams) is exploited by RomCom, Paper Werewolf and Sandworm in ESET APT Report Q2-Q3 2025.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/videos/who-where-how-apt-attacks-q2-2025-q3-2025/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/update-winrar-tools-now-romcom-and-others-exploiting-zero-day-vulnerability/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-8088
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.t1203
  - cve.2025.8088
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\winrar.exe'
      - '\rar.exe'
      - '\unrar.exe'
      - '\unrar64.exe'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - User extracting a legitimate .lnk into Startup manually (extremely rare)
level: high
3481.spl:
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","WinRAR.exe") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where NOT match(file_name, "(?i)\\.lnk$")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
3481.datadog: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\WinRAR.exe OR *\winrar.exe OR *\Rar.exe OR *\rar.exe OR *\UnRAR.exe OR *\unrar.exe OR *\UnRAR64.exe OR *\unrar64.exe) @TargetFilename:(*"\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\"* OR *"\\start menu\\programs\\startup\\"*)
3481.falcon:

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())

3484.def:
// CVE-2025-8088 / RomCom — archive utility silently writes a persistence artefact
// into the per-user Startup folder during what looks like a routine extraction.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip32.exe","winzip64.exe","wzzip.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where FileName endswith ".lnk"
      or FileName endswith ".dll"
      or FileName endswith ".exe"
      or FileName endswith ".bat"
      or FileName endswith ".cmd"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Archiver = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ArchiverCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          DroppedFile = FileName,
          DroppedPath = FolderPath,
          SHA256, MD5, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
3484.sent:
// CVE-2025-8088 / RomCom — same intent on Sentinel via ASIM ImFileEvent
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip32.exe","winzip64.exe","wzzip.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".lnk"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
      or TargetFileName endswith ".exe"

3498.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — s1ngularity: Popular Nx Build System Package Compromised with Data-Stealing Malw
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("telemetry.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/inventory.txt", "/tmp/inventory.txt.bak", "/tmp/pr-message.txt", "/usr/bin/env") or FileName in~ ("telemetry.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
3498.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — s1ngularity: Popular Nx Build System Package Compromised with Data-Stealing Malw ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("telemetry.js"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/inventory.txt*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/inventory.txt.bak*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/pr-message.txt*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/usr/bin/env*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("telemetry.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

3499.def:
// s1ngularity: AI CLI launched with safety-bypass flags as part of credential recon
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("claude","gemini","q")
   or FolderPath endswith "/claude" or FolderPath endswith "/gemini" or FolderPath endswith "/q"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dangerously-skip-permissions","--yolo","--trust-all-tools")
// the s1ngularity prompt writes to /tmp/inventory.txt — boosts confidence when present
| extend HasInventoryPrompt = ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/inventory.txt" or ProcessCommandLine has "keystore" or ProcessCommandLine has "metamask"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          HasInventoryPrompt, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
3499.sent:
// s1ngularity: AI CLI launched with safety-bypass flags — ASIM cross-vendor
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("claude","gemini","q")
   or TargetProcessName endswith "/claude" or TargetProcessName endswith "/gemini" or TargetProcessName endswith "/q"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dangerously-skip-permissions","--yolo","--trust-all-tools")
| extend HasInventoryPrompt = TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/inventory.txt" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "keystore" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "metamask"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, HasInventoryPrompt

title: s1ngularity nx — AI CLI Assistant Invoked with Permission-Bypass Flags
id: 7d7e44b1-4f1e-4d3e-9c2d-1f5a8a3b9e7c
status: experimental
description: Detects developer AI CLIs (Claude, Gemini, Amazon Q) launched with safety-disabling flags as observed in the s1ngularity nx npm supply-chain attack (Aug 2025), where the malicious telemetry.js script weaponised local AI assistants for credential / wallet reconnaissance.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-security-alert-popular-nx-build-system-package-compromised-with-data-stealing-malware
  - https://github.com/nrwl/nx/security/advisories/GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c
  - https://socket.dev/blog/nx-packages-compromised
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2025/08/28
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1119
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/claude'
      - '/gemini'
      - '/q'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--dangerously-skip-permissions'
      - '--yolo'
      - '--trust-all-tools'
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags
falsepositives:
  - Developers intentionally running AI CLIs in agent / autonomous mode for legitimate work — should be rare and reviewable.
level: high
3499.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("claude","gemini","q") OR Processes.process IN ("*claude *","*gemini *","* q chat *")) AND (Processes.process="*--dangerously-skip-permissions*" OR Processes.process="*--yolo*" OR Processes.process="*--trust-all-tools*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
3499.datadog: (source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:windows.sysmon) @process.executable.path:(*/claude OR */gemini OR */q OR */claude.exe OR */gemini.exe) @process.command_line:(*--dangerously-skip-permissions* OR *--yolo* OR *--trust-all-tools*)
